_comment: Counterfactual check: drop the dose from the improved smoking claim and ask what the study no longer commits to measuring.

stem.en: Suppose the improved claim lost its dose and read: "Smoking causes lung cancer in 10 per cent of smokers after 20 years." Compared with the full claim, which measurement would the study no longer be committed to making?

text.en: The number of years each person had smoked before diagnosis
The number of cigarettes each person smoked in a typical day
Whether each person in the study had lung cancer at the end
Whether each person in the study was a smoker or a non-smoker

explanation.en: The dose-response part ("30-40 cigarettes a day") is what commits the study to measuring cigarettes per day. Without it, smoking is only yes or no; years of smoking are still needed for the time-response, and lung cancer is still the outcome.

hints.en: Each part of the claim commits the study to one measurement. Which part was removed?
